title: 1.1.1 What Is Programming / Software Lifecycle
description: Learn what a program is, explore the SDLC, and write your first JavaScript using console.log().

steps.title: Hello, world!
steps.instructions:
A **program** is a set of instructions that tells a computer what to do. **JavaScript** is the programming language you'll use this year.

Let's write your first instruction. In `script.js`, under the Step 1 comment, type:

```js
console.log("Hello, world!");
```

`console.log()` tells the computer to print whatever is inside the parentheses. Check the console panel below to see your output.
hints: Make sure you use straight quotes ("), not curly quotes.
Don't forget the semicolon at the end.

steps.title: Print a number
steps.instructions:
JavaScript can do math. Under the Step 2 comment, type:

```js
console.log(2 + 2);
```

Notice there are **no quotes** around `2 + 2`. That's because numbers aren't text — JavaScript calculates the answer and prints the result.

Try changing the numbers or using other operators: `-`, `*`, `/`.
hints: Numbers don't need quotes. Text (strings) do.

steps.title: Join two strings
steps.instructions:
Text values in JavaScript are called **strings**. You can join two strings together with `+`. Under the Step 3 comment, type:

```js
console.log("My name is " + "a programmer!");
```

This is called **concatenation**. Notice the space after "is " — without it the words smash together.
hints: Both sides of the + must be in quotes.
If your output looks like 'My name isa programmer!' you forgot the space.

steps.title: True or false
steps.instructions:
JavaScript can compare values and tell you if something is true or false. Under the Step 4 comment, type:

```js
console.log(100 > 50);
```

The output is `true` — a **boolean** value. Booleans are either `true` or `false`. Try `console.log(10 < 5);` to see `false`.
hints: Booleans don't have quotes — they're not strings.

steps.title: Print your name
steps.instructions:
Now make it personal. Under the Step 5 comment, print your own name:

```js
console.log("Your Name Here");
```

Replace "Your Name Here" with your actual name.
hints: Keep the quotes around your name — it's a string.

steps.title: Print your hobby
steps.instructions:
Under the Step 6 comment, print your favorite hobby:

```js
console.log("I love building robots.");
```

Your program now has **6 lines of code** — each one an instruction the computer follows **in order**, top to bottom. This is called **sequential execution**.

You just wrote your first JavaScript program!
hints: Each console.log() goes on its own line.
Put your actual hobby inside the quotes.
